findings.observation: Sheet 8 (Existing Conditions & Demolition Plan) shows the street names with ROW designation: 'KINNEY AVENUE (R.O.W. VARIES)', 'COLLIER STREET (R.O.W. VARIES)', and 'NASH AVENUE (R.O.W. VARIES)'. Vision analysis of Sheet 8 confirmed that the streets are labeled but stated: 'No specific numeric measurements (e.g., "50' ROW" or "60' ROW") are dimensioned for the overall width of these streets on this sheet. Instead of a specific measurement, the plans explicitly use the text label "(R.O.W. VARIES)".' Sheet 13 also shows similar labeling. No sheets in the plan set provide specific numeric dimensions for the existing ROW widths.
findings.reasoning: The checklist item requires that existing ROW width be both 'shown' and 'dimensioned'. While the streets are labeled and the ROW is acknowledged as existing, the text '(R.O.W. VARIES)' is a qualitative statement rather than a dimension. The CC Submittal Checklist (GRD-01) requires dimensioned ROW widths on the existing conditions sheet. The lack of specific numeric dimensions (e.g., '60' ROW', '80' ROW') constitutes a deficiency.
findings.explanation: Existing ROW widths are labeled as 'varies' but not dimensioned with specific measurements on existing conditions sheets
findings.resolution: Provide specific numeric dimensions for existing ROW widths for Kinney Avenue, Collier Street, Nash Avenue, and South Lamar Boulevard on the existing conditions sheets (Sheets 8-9).

findings.observation: Sheets 21-22 (Grading Plan 1 of 2 and 2 of 2) show existing and proposed behind-the-curb improvements. Vision analysis of Sheet 22 confirmed: 'The plan shows proposed sidewalk paths along the street frontages...The legend specifically includes a diagonal hatch pattern labeled exactly as "PROPOSED ADA PATH"...The legend contains a stippled/dotted hatch pattern labeled "PROPOSED LANDSCAPE AREA (SEE LANDSCAPE SHEETS FOR DETAILS)"...The plan also shows existing trees in these areas. The legend includes a tree symbol labeled "EXISTING TREES TO REMAIN (SEE TREE PRESERVATION PLAN & COORDINATE WITH LANDSCAPE ARCHITECT)". Several of these symbols are drawn along the Collier Street and South Lamar Boulevard frontages.' Sheet 21 legend shows symbols for proposed ADA paths, landscape areas, and existing trees to remain.
findings.reasoning: Behind-the-curb improvements include sidewalks, landscape strips, trees, lighting, and work between the curb and property line. The grading plans show proposed sidewalks/ADA paths, proposed landscape areas in the parkway zones, and existing trees to remain along street frontages. The plans also show the distinction between existing pavement tie-ins and proposed improvements, and existing vs proposed contours and elevations in ROW areas. This satisfies the requirement to show both existing and proposed behind-the-curb improvements.
findings.explanation: Grading plans (Sheets 21-22) show existing trees to remain, proposed sidewalks/ADA paths, and proposed landscape areas in ROW

findings.observation: Sheets 21-22 (Grading Plan) show both existing and proposed grade lines. The legend on both sheets clearly defines 'EXISTING CONTOURS' (dashed lines labeled with numbers like 535, 540) and 'PROPOSED CONTOURS' (solid lines with numbers in parentheses like (535), (540)). The legend also differentiates between 'PROPOSED SPOT ELEVATION' (with notation like '533.00') and 'EXISTING SPOT ELEVATION' (with notation like '+EX 533.00'). Both sheets show extensive contour lines and spot elevations throughout the site and ROW areas, illustrating the existing terrain and proposed grading changes.
findings.reasoning: A grading plan must show both existing and proposed grade lines to demonstrate how the site's topography will change. The plans clearly distinguish between existing conditions (dashed contours, +EX spot elevations) and proposed conditions (solid contours in parentheses, proposed spot elevations). This allows reviewers to understand the grading impacts and drainage patterns. The requirement is satisfied.
findings.explanation: Sheets 21-22 show existing contours (dashed) and proposed contours (solid/parentheses), plus existing and proposed spot elevations with clear legend distinctions

findings.observation: Sheet 14 (Dimensional Control & Site Plan 1 Of 2) shows dimensions for ROW improvements. Vision analysis confirmed: 'Along Collier Street (top of plan), there are dimensioned zones typical for Austin streetscapes: "5' PLANTING ZONE" and "6' CLEAR ZONE" (This zone typically serves as the primary pedestrian sidewalk path). Along Kinney Avenue (left side of plan), there is a label indicating an "8' SIDEWALK". At the entrance off Collier Street...there is a width dimension of "22'" indicating the driveway width. At the entrance off Kinney Avenue...there is a width dimension of "20'" indicating the driveway width.' The sheet also includes a Record Curve Table with curve radii and lengths for ROW curves. Per the validation methodology, dimensions do not need to be on a specific sheet—they just need to exist somewhere in the plan set.
findings.reasoning: The validation methodology specifically notes that ROW improvement dimensions should not be required on any specific sheet, and on larger sites dimension control plans typically show these dimensions. Sheet 14 serves this purpose and provides width dimensions for sidewalk zones (5' planting + 6' clear = 11' total along Collier; 8' along Kinney), driveway widths (20' and 22'), and curve dimensions for ROW features. This satisfies the requirement that dimensions for new or modified ROW improvements be shown somewhere in the plan set.
findings.explanation: Sheet 14 shows ROW improvement dimensions including sidewalk widths (5' planting zone, 6' clear zone, 8' sidewalk), driveway widths (20', 22'), and curve dimensions

findings.observation: Review of the site plan sheets and README indicates no new public roadway construction is proposed. The project proposes a mixed-use development with on-site circulation, driveways connecting to existing streets (Collier Street, South Lamar Boulevard, Kinney Avenue), and ROW improvements (sidewalks, driveway aprons). However, no new public streets are being constructed, and existing street alignments are not being modified. Sheets 13, 14, 15 show site access via driveways but no new roadway construction. The facts.md file notes ROW dedication along Collier Street and Kinney Avenue, but this is land dedication, not roadway construction.
findings.reasoning: This item's condition is 'If new roadway construction proposed'. New roadway construction refers to building new public streets or significantly reconstructing existing roadways with plan and profile views. The project includes on-site driveways and private circulation, but these are not public roadways requiring the engineering documentation specified in this checklist item (horizontal/vertical views per roadway construction standards). Since no new public roadway is being constructed, the condition is not met.
findings.explanation: No new public roadway construction is proposed; project includes only on-site driveways and circulation connecting to existing streets

findings.observation: As established for CC-23-05, no new public roadway construction is proposed. The project includes on-site driveways and private circulation but no new public streets requiring target speed designation per TCM roadway construction standards.
findings.reasoning: Target speed is a roadway design parameter required for new public roadway construction, as it drives geometry, sight distance, and signage/striping requirements per the Technical Criteria Manual (TCM). Since no new public roadways are being constructed (only on-site driveways and private circulation), the condition 'If new roadway construction proposed' is not met, and this item does not apply.
findings.explanation: No new public roadway construction proposed; target speed requirements do not apply to on-site driveways

findings.observation: Review of the plan set shows ROW improvements including sidewalks, driveway aprons, and ADA paths along existing streets (Collier Street, South Lamar Boulevard, Kinney Avenue, Evergreen Avenue). Sheet 13 (Overall Site & Paving & Striping Plan) shows on-site paving and striping. Sheet 31 shows pavement marking details for striping and fire lanes. However, these improvements are site access features (driveways) and pedestrian facilities (sidewalks), not new or modified roadways requiring signage and striping plans. The existing public streets themselves (travel lanes, lane configurations) are not being modified or reconstructed.
findings.reasoning: The condition states 'If new roadway construction or work in ROW'. While there IS work in ROW (sidewalks, driveway aprons), the specific deficiency described is 'Signage and striping plan not provided for new or modified roadway in ROW'. The work in ROW consists of pedestrian facilities and driveway connections, not modification of the roadway itself (travel lanes, lane striping, traffic control). Signage and striping plans are required when the roadway pavement, lane configuration, or traffic control is modified. Since the existing street travel ways are not being reconstructed or restriped, this item does not apply.
findings.explanation: ROW improvements are sidewalks and driveway aprons; no new or modified roadway travel lanes requiring signage/striping plans

findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Grading Plan 1 of 2) shows proposed low profile walls with top and bottom elevations. Vision analysis confirmed: 'Yes, specific top and bottom wall elevations are explicitly called out...In the bottom right portion of the plan, near the southern property boundary adjacent to the "SAGE CONDOMINIUMS" tract, there are multiple callouts providing these elevations. Exact transcriptions include: "TW 548.50 / BW 547.00", "TW 548.75 / BW 547.50", "TW 548.25 / BW 546.75" (TW typically stands for Top of Wall, and BW stands for Bottom of Wall).' The legend on Sheet 21 shows 'PROPOSED LOW PROFILE WALLS' as a specific line type. Sheet 48 (Hardscape Details) provides construction details for retaining walls with note 'HEIGHT VARIES REF GRADING PLAN'.
findings.reasoning: The condition is 'If retaining walls >2 feet proposed'. The grading plan shows retaining walls with TW/BW elevations marked. The heights shown are approximately 1.5 feet (548.50-547.00=1.5'), 1.25 feet (548.75-547.50=1.25'), and 1.5 feet (548.25-546.75=1.5'). These are labeled as 'low profile walls', and all measured heights are under 2 feet. While the Sheet 48 detail notes 'HEIGHT VARIES', the specific walls shown on the grading plan with elevations are all under the 2-foot threshold. Since the walls shown exceed the minimum threshold for documentation (they are shown with elevations), and the condition requires walls >2 feet, this item is satisfied by the walls that exist. However, if ANY walls exceed 2 feet, top and bottom elevations must be shown for those walls. The documentation provided shows elevations for the walls present, satisfying the requirement.
findings.explanation: Sheet 21 shows retaining walls with top and bottom elevations labeled (TW/BW notation with specific elevations like TW 548.50 / BW 547.00)

findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows proposed low profile retaining walls along the Collier Street frontage. Vision analysis noted: 'There appears to be a wall associated with the frontage improvements here...It runs adjacent to a curved sidewalk area labeled "PROPOSED VARIABLE WIDTH PUBLIC SIDEWALK EASEMENT". While it is associated with the street frontage improvements, it appears to sit just inside the property line or within the easement rather than directly inside the standard street ROW.' Sheet 48 (Hardscape Details) shows a typical retaining wall detail with construction specifications but includes note 'REF. STRUCTURAL DRAWINGS FOR ALL CONCRETE PLANTER REINFORCEMENT', which applies to planters, not the site retaining walls. No sealed structural drawings specific to the site retaining walls were found in the plan set. The validation methodology specifies this requirement applies only to walls 'in the right-of-way, easements, and any City property' per TCM 13.1.0.
findings.reasoning: Per the validation methodology and TCM 13.1.0, sealed structural drawings are required specifically for retaining walls 'in the right-of-way, easements, and any City property.' The walls shown on Sheet 21 appear to be within or adjacent to the 'VARIABLE WIDTH PUBLIC SIDEWALK EASEMENT', which is a public easement. If these walls are in a public easement and exceed 2 feet in height, sealed structural drawings would be required. The Sheet 48 detail is a typical construction detail, not a sealed structural drawing. The measured heights from Sheet 21 (approximately 1.25-1.5 feet) appear to be below the 2-foot threshold, which would make this requirement not applicable. However, Sheet 48 notes 'HEIGHT VARIES REF GRADING PLAN', suggesting some walls may exceed 2 feet. Given that walls exist in or near public easements and the validation methodology specifically addresses this scenario, and no sealed structural drawings are present, this is a potential deficiency if any walls >2 feet are in ROW/easements. However, based on the specific measurements shown, all walls appear to be low-profile (<2 feet), making the condition not met.
findings.explanation: Retaining walls shown on grading plan are low-profile (<2 feet based on TW/BW dimensions); condition requires walls >2 feet

findings.observation: Vision analysis of Sheet 15 (Dimensional Control & Site Plan 2 Of 2) confirmed: 'Near the lower center of the layout for "PROPOSED BUILDING 1," there is a specific designated area labeled for trash. The plan includes a leader line pointing to an interior space with the exact text: "TRASH ROOM SEE ARCHITECTURAL PLANS FOR DETAILS"'. Vision analysis of Sheet 14 found no dumpster or trash locations. Semantic search for 'dumpster garbage cart waste container trash collection location' returned 9 results, with the most relevant being Sheet 5 notes about dumpster placement requirements (compatibility standards requiring dumpsters 20 feet from SF-5 or more restrictive zoning) and Sheet 39 (Building Plan Level 3) description mentioning 'trash rooms'.
findings.reasoning: The checklist item requires that locations of existing and proposed dumpsters and garbage carts (interior or exterior) be shown on the site plan. Sheet 15 clearly labels an interior 'TRASH ROOM' with a callout, identifying the location. This satisfies the requirement to show the location of trash collection areas. While the label references architectural plans for details, the location is shown on the civil site plan as required. No existing dumpsters are shown (the existing buildings are to be demolished per Sheet 8).
findings.explanation: Sheet 15 shows interior trash room location with label 'TRASH ROOM SEE ARCHITECTURAL PLANS FOR DETAILS' on the site plan

findings.observation: Sheet 13 (Overall Site & Paving & Striping Plan) shows proposed work in and adjacent to the ROW. Vision analysis confirmed: 'Several improvements are shown encroaching into or adjacent to the R.O.W., including: Driveways: A driveway connecting to Collier Street is explicitly labeled "PROPOSED TYPE II DRIVEWAY (SEE DETAIL SHEET 30)"...Sidewalks/ADA Paths: A "5' SIDEWALK" is labeled along the Collier Street frontage...The distinction is made graphically rather than with explicit text notes. The "PROPERTY LINE" is clearly defined in the Legend...Work depicted outside of this Property Line and within the designated street areas (like South Lamar Blvd and Collier St) is visually indicated as being within the R.O.W. The "LIMITS OF CONSTRUCTION" (defined in the Legend as a dashed line with an "L") is shown extending past the Property Line and into the R.O.W. areas to encompass the proposed driveways, sidewalks, and pavement tie-ins, clearly indicating that construction activities will occur within the public Right-of-Way.'
findings.reasoning: The requirement is that proposed work adjacent to or encroaching into ROW be identified and labeled. Sheet 13 shows the limits of construction extending into ROW areas and labels specific improvements (sidewalks, driveways, ADA paths). The property line and ROW boundaries are clearly delineated, and improvements within the ROW are labeled by type (e.g., 'PROPOSED TYPE II DRIVEWAY', '5' SIDEWALK', 'PROPOSED ADA PATH'). The use of 'LIMITS OF CONSTRUCTION' extending into the ROW graphically identifies that work will occur in the ROW. This satisfies the requirement to identify and label ROW work.
findings.explanation: Sheet 13 shows limits of construction extending into ROW and labels improvements (driveways, sidewalks, ADA paths) with property line clearly delineated

summary: 10 of 11 items pass, 1 fails: existing ROW widths not dimensioned with specific numeric measurements (CC-23-01). Items CC-23-05, CC-23-06, CC-23-07 (new roadway construction requirements) and CC-23-09 (structural drawings for tall retaining walls) are not applicable to this project.
